clue.text: Engaged with number due at ground made less

parts.note: engaged in something is 'at' it, as in at work or at war
ten is a number

indicators.note: ground means crushed and reduced to a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone engaged with a sum that is due at the ground, which has been reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is the anagram signal, rearranging DUE AT; 'Engaged' gives AT, as one is 'at' a task.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something thinned, weakened or reduced has been made less.

clue.text: Ottoman, light-hearted, with FT reproduced one from 3 27 7 down

indicators.note: reproduced means made again in a new form, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the hyphen
taken as written: the newspaper's initials

explanation.surface: A cheerful Turk reprinted alongside the Financial Times, with a nod to a famous author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduced' rearranges all twenty-one letters of OTTOMAN, LIGHTHEARTED and FT. The definition points to the author at 3, 27, 7 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this 1918 lost-world adventure novel is one of Edgar Rice Burroughs's books.

clue.text: Author changes rubric agreed by rowdy sons

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the two words that follow are switched around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
rowdy means rough, boisterous
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A writer alters the printed rules his unruly boys have accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns RUBRIC AGREED into EDGARRICEBUR, then ROUGH and S finish the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the American writer who created Tarzan is an author.

clue.text: Posh Rod gripped by news as implied

parts.note: U is the crossword abbreviation for upper-class, posh

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside, so the rod goes between the letters for news

parts.note: news read as the plural of new: two Ns, N being the abbreviation for new
a spoke is a rod in a wheel

explanation.surface: An upper-class man called Rod is caught up in the headlines, by implication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is the plural of 'new', so two Ns, which hold SPOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something implied is understood without being said in words.

clue.text: Our publication in Nazareth, as Poe recollected, one from 3 27 7 down

indicators.note: in places the paper's initials inside the rearranged letters
recollected read as re-collected, gathered again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
FT, the Financial Times, is the publication carrying this crossword

explanation.surface: The newspaper appears in Nazareth, as remembered by Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' is the anagram signal, read as re-collected; 'in' places the paper's initials. The definition points to the author at 3, 27, 7 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the 1912 jungle novel was the first of Burroughs's many books about his ape-raised hero.

clue.text: Cattle worker departs with rambler

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
a rover is one who wanders, a rambler

explanation.surface: A cowhand leaves along with a hiker.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a drover drives herds of cattle or sheep to market, a stock worker.

clue.text: Wicked soul emptied safe

parts.note: in ancient Egyptian belief the ba is the soul

indicators.note: emptied means the inside letters are removed, leaving only the first and last

explanation.surface: An evil person cleaned out the strongbox.
explanation.walkthrough: BA, the Egyptian soul, is a crossword staple; 'emptied' leaves SE from 'safe'. 'safe' tempts as the definition (a safe base), but 'Wicked' is it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: base as an adjective means morally low, contemptible.

clue.text: See 3
Screen star in final appearance finally disappearing

indicators.note: finally disappearing says the closing letter of the phrase drops away

parts.note: a swansong is a last performance or final appearance

explanation.surface: A film star in a farewell role, fading at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally disappearing' drops the last letter, G, from SWANSONG. Gloria Swanson starred in Sunset Boulevard.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Gloria Swanson was a Hollywood film star of the silent era and beyond.

clue.text: One composing letter after a bit of work

parts.note: the letter after A in the alphabet is B
an erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A writer drafting a letter after finishing a bit of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter after' looks like a charade order, but it means the letter that follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer, so one who composes music.

clue.text: Newly sober actor modified language

indicators.note: newly means made afresh, so the first word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters of the second word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recently sober actor changes the way he speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly' turns SOBER into SERBO and 'modified' turns ACTOR into CROAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this was the shared tongue of the former Yugoslavia, a language.

clue.text: Locks process keeps one in violent job-centre

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the numeral goes into the word for violent

parts.note: hard can mean violent, as in a hard blow
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone getting through things at an aggressive job centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'job-centre' reads as the UK benefits office but gives the middle letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a styled arrangement of the hair is the result of treating one's locks.

clue.text: Hostelry in which a bloodsucker gets to drink — what?

indicators.note: gets to drink means takes in, so the query word goes inside

parts.note: a louse is a bloodsucking parasite
eh is said for what? when one has not heard

explanation.surface: A pub where a parasite is allowed a drink, to general bafflement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what' is a query word here, the sort of thing said when one has not heard; 'gets to drink' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hostelry is an inn, and a pub serving beer is one.

clue.text: Stick with date hero revised

indicators.note: revised means changed, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Keep seeing a romantic partner whose role has been rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to stick with a plan is to keep to it faithfully.

clue.text: Relate to male secretary — this to fill essential need?

indicators.note: to fill means to go inside, so these pieces are put between the middle letters
essential means at the core, so the central letters are taken

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting on with a male secretary: is this meeting a basic need?
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential' takes the core letters of 'need'; 'to fill' sends the other pieces inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to relate to someone is to share and understand their feelings.

clue.text: Dead good with United

parts.note: united things are made one

explanation.surface: A football supporter's lament: good players gone, and United done for.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphemism: someone who has gone has passed away.

clue.text: Flustered female trapped by Tory's exploited

indicators.note: trapped by means caught between, so the letter for female sits inside

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory; the 's is no letter
used means exploited

explanation.surface: A woman is rattled after being cornered and used by a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone flustered is bewildered and muddled.

clue.text: Some llamas approach with all haste

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few llamas head this way at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: as soon as possible means with all speed.

clue.text: Lively parts from singer unknown in South Island

indicators.note: in puts the singer and the unknown between the two abbreviations

parts.note: Cher is a famous American singer
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Bright passages by a mystery singer recorded in New Zealand's South Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Island' looks like New Zealand's island but is two abbreviations around CHER and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Music term: scherzi are the quick, playful movements of a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Fly useful in these rivers to halve odds in Test

indicators.note: to halve means to split apart, so the rivers go between the two letters
odds in picks the first and third letters of the word

parts.note: R for river, the Ouse, and R again: three rivers

explanation.surface: A fishing fly suited to these rivers, splitting odds in a cricket Test.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is an English river and R abbreviates river; the odd letters of 'Test' are T and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic hint: a fly is the zip opening on the front of a pair of these garments.

clue.text: King loves hawk to eliminate completely

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, Latin rex
love is zero in tennis, O, so loves is two Os
to tout is to hawk goods

explanation.surface: A monarch adores selling, keen to wipe out the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to root something out is to get rid of it entirely.

clue.text: Pages in black and white only just done!

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for pages inside the word for piebald

parts.note: pied means patched in black and white, like a magpie

explanation.surface: Black and white pages, barely finished!
explanation.walkthrough: 'only just done' means narrowly beaten, done in the sense of defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be beaten by a whisker is to be narrowly defeated, only just done.

clue.text: See 3
Wants information about English XI getting runs
